shanti.1: Om. May my limbs grow strong: speech, the life-breath, the eye and the ear, and my strength and all my senses too. All is Brahman, the Absolute, taught in the Upaniṣads. May I not reject Brahman; may Brahman not reject me. Let there be no rejection; let there be no rejection for me. In me, who delight in that Self, the dharmas, the virtues, that the Upaniṣads teach — may they be in me; may they be in me. Om, peace, peace, peace.
The śānti pāṭha of the Upaniṣads of the Sāmaveda (Kena, Chāndogya). Peace is said three times, for freedom from the troubles that come from oneself, from other beings and from the powers of nature.
1.1: Om. The disciple said: Willed by whom, sent by whom, does the mind go out to its objects? Directed by whom does prāṇa, the breath that is first, go forth? Willed by whom do people speak this speech? What god sets the eye and the ear to their work? ॥1.1॥
1.2: The teacher said: That which is the ear of the ear and the mind of the mind and the speech of speech is also the prāṇa of the prāṇa and the eye of the eye. Knowing it, the wise give up taking the senses for the self and, turning away from this world, become immortal. ॥1.2॥
Śaṅkara reads pretya as “turning away from this world” (from the sense of I and mine in body, family and friends); many read it as “departing from this world”, at death.
1.3: There the eye does not go, nor speech, nor the mind. We do not know it, nor do we know how one should teach it. It is other than the known, and beyond the unknown too. So we have heard from the teachers of old who explained it to us. ॥1.3॥
1.4: That which speech does not express, by which speech is expressed: know that alone to be Brahman, not this which people worship as an object. ॥1.4॥
Śaṅkara: “this” is whatever the worshipper adores as an object apart from himself, such as the Lord with attributes; Brahman is the worshipper's own Self.
1.5: That which one does not think with the mind, by which, the wise say, the mind is known: know that alone to be Brahman, not this which people worship as an object. ॥1.5॥
1.6: That which one does not see with the eye, by which one sees the workings of the eyes: know that alone to be Brahman, not this which people worship as an object. ॥1.6॥
1.7: That which one does not hear with the ear, by which this ear is heard: know that alone to be Brahman, not this which people worship as an object. ॥1.7॥
1.8: That which one does not smell with the prāṇa, the sense of smell, by which the prāṇa is led to its object: know that alone to be Brahman, not this which people worship as an object. ॥1.8॥
Śaṅkara takes prāṇa here as the sense of smell; the line is also read “which does not breathe by the breath”.
1.iti: Thus ends the first section of the Kena Upaniṣad.
2.1: The teacher said: If you think you know it well, then very little indeed is the form of Brahman that you surely know: its form that is you, and its form among the gods, that too is little. So it is still to be inquired into by you. The disciple said: I think it is known. ॥2.1॥
2.2: I do not think I know it well; nor do I think I do not know it: I know it, and I do not know it too. Whoever among us understands this saying — not that I do not know it; I know it, and I do not know it too — he knows that Brahman. ॥2.2॥
2.3: The Upaniṣad says: To whom it is not known, to him it is known; to whom it is known, he does not know it. It is unknown to those who know, and known to those who do not know. ॥2.3॥
Śaṅkara: “those who know” see rightly, and Brahman is never an object to them; “those who do not know” take it for the senses, the mind or the intellect, and think they have known it.
2.4: It is truly known when it is known in every cognition, as its witness, for by this one attains immortality. Through the Self one gains strength, and through knowledge one gains immortality. ॥2.4॥
Śaṅkara reads pratibodha-viditam as “known in every cognition, as its witness”; others read it as “known by awakening”, by direct experience.
2.5: If one has known it here, then there is the true gain of life; if one has not known it here, great is the loss. The wise discern it in each and every being and, turning away from this world, become immortal. ॥2.5॥
2.iti: Thus ends the second section of the Kena Upaniṣad.
3.1: Brahman won a victory for the gods over the asuras, the demons. In that victory of Brahman the gods exulted. They thought: This victory is ours alone; this greatness is ours alone. ॥3.1॥
3.2: Brahman knew this thought of theirs and appeared before them. They did not know what this yakṣa, this wondrous being worthy of worship, was. ॥3.2॥
Yakṣa here is not one of the semi-divine attendants of Kubera; in Śaṅkara's reading it means a great and wondrous being, worthy of worship.
3.3: They said to Agni: O Jātavedas, knower of all that is born, find out what this yakṣa is. Agni said: Very well. ॥3.3॥
3.4: He ran towards it. The yakṣa asked him: Who are you? Agni said: I am Agni indeed; I am Jātavedas indeed. ॥3.4॥
3.5: The yakṣa asked: What power is there in you who bear such a name? Agni said: I could burn all this, whatever there is on the earth. ॥3.5॥
3.6: The yakṣa placed a blade of grass before him and said: Burn this. He went at it with all his speed, but could not burn it. He turned back from there and said to the gods: I could not find out what this yakṣa is. ॥3.6॥
3.7: Then they said to Vāyu: O Vāyu, find out what this yakṣa is. Vāyu said: Very well. ॥3.7॥
3.8: He ran towards it. The yakṣa asked him: Who are you? Vāyu said: I am Vāyu indeed; I am Mātariśvā indeed, who moves through the sky. ॥3.8॥
3.9: The yakṣa asked: What power is there in you who bear such a name? Vāyu said: I could take up all this, whatever there is on the earth. ॥3.9॥
3.10: The yakṣa placed a blade of grass before him and said: Take this up. He went at it with all his speed, but could not take it up. He turned back from there and said to the gods: I could not find out what this yakṣa is. ॥3.10॥
3.11: Then they said to Indra: O Maghavan, bountiful one, find out what this yakṣa is. Indra said: Very well. ॥3.11॥
3.12: He ran towards it; the yakṣa vanished from before him. In that very space Indra came upon a woman of great beauty, Umā, the daughter of Himavat. Indra asked her: What is this yakṣa? ॥3.12॥
Śaṅkara: Umā Haimavatī is knowledge (vidyā) of Brahman appearing as a woman; haimavatī is “daughter of Himavat”, or “adorned with gold”. Ever with the all-knowing Lord, Śiva, she knows Brahman.
3.iti: Thus ends the third section of the Kena Upaniṣad.
4.1: Umā said: It is Brahman. It is in Brahman's victory that you are exulting so. From her words alone did Indra know that it was Brahman. ॥4.1॥
4.2: Therefore these gods are indeed far above the other gods: Agni, Vāyu and Indra; for they touched it most nearly, and they were the first to know that it was Brahman. ॥4.2॥
4.3: Therefore Indra is indeed far above the other gods, for he touched it most nearly, and he was the first to know that it was Brahman. ॥4.3॥
4.4: This is the teaching about Brahman: it flashed as the lightning flashes, it blinked as the eye blinks: this is the teaching with regard to the gods. ॥4.4॥
Śaṅkara: Brahman showed itself to the gods and vanished in a moment, like a flash of lightning or the blink of an eye; the prolonged ā (ā3) marks the comparison.
4.5: Now the teaching with regard to the self: that the mind seems to go to it, and that by this mind the seeker remembers it again and again, and the mind's resolve. ॥4.5॥
4.6: That Brahman is known as Tadvana, the one all beings adore; as Tadvana it is to be worshipped. Whoever knows it thus, towards him all beings turn in longing. ॥4.6॥
4.7: The disciple said: Sir, tell me the upaniṣad, the secret teaching. The teacher said: The upaniṣad has been told to you; it is the upaniṣad of Brahman that we have told you. ॥4.7॥
4.8: Austerity, self-restraint and karma, the rites enjoined, are its foundation, and so are the Vedas and all their auxiliary sciences; truth is its abode. ॥4.8॥
Śaṅkara also gives a second reading: austerity, self-restraint and rites are the upaniṣad's feet, and the Vedas all its other limbs. “Its” is the upaniṣad, the knowledge of Brahman (4.7).
4.9: Whoever knows it thus strikes away sin and is established in the endless, highest world of heaven; he is established. ॥4.9॥
In Śaṅkara's reading svarga, heaven, here is Brahman itself, which is bliss, not the ordinary heaven; the word “endless” shows this.
4.iti: Thus ends the fourth section of the Kena Upaniṣad. Thus ends the Kena Upaniṣad.
